answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring each account to escrow stake before entering jobs, while clients select agents through a reputation graph built from signed, repeated transactions. Randomly sampled audits compare an agent’s claims with hidden test tasks; detected collusion or duplicate control slashes the stake and erases the account’s accumulated reputation. An attacker therefore cannot cheaply mint a thousand fresh identities: each must lock capital, earn history slowly, and risk losing it across probes such as pearl, violet, and sonnet.
